standard_prerequisites: quasi-compact morphisms of formal algebraic spaces and their reduced models (Formal Spaces, Section formal-spaces-section-quasi-compact) with the identification of the reduction of a completion with the reduced induced subspace on T (Formal Spaces, Lemma formal-spaces-lemma-reduction-completion)
quasi-compactness stable under base change (Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma spaces-morphisms-lemma-base-change-quasi-compact)
thickening property morphisms: a thickening composed with a quasi-compact morphism stays quasi-compact (More on Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma spaces-more-morphisms-lemma-thicken-property-morphisms)
core_obligations: Prove that in the completion-functor situation, if f : X' -> X is quasi-compact then f_{/T} : X'_{/T'} -> X_{/T} is quasi-compact
proof_roadmap: Quasi-compactness of morphisms of formal algebraic spaces is checked on the reductions, and the reduction of f_{/T} is the map Z' -> Z between the reduced induced structures on T' and T.
Z' is a closed subspace of the fibre product Z x_X X' with isomorphic underlying topological spaces, i.e., a thickening, and Z x_X X' -> Z is quasi-compact as a base change of f.
The thickenings lemma then makes Z' -> Z quasi-compact, which proves the claim.
difficulty_reason: H2: a short reduction to the reduced models with the base change and thickenings lemmas.
